questions: Does the function modify the text by replacing spaces with underscores in the words from mystrings only once per occurrence, or should it replace overlapping matches recursively (e.g., if 'a b' and 'b c' are in mystrings, and text contains 'a b c', what happens)?
Should the function treat punctuation as part of words (e.g., 'world!' in tests) or strip punctuation before counting frequency?
Is the order of words on the x-axis based on first appearance in the modified text, or alphabetical, or arbitrary (e.g., Counter order)?
Are the replacements applied sequentially in the order of mystrings, and if so, does later replacement operate on the already-modified text (potentially creating new underscores)?
Should the function split the modified text by whitespace to get words, or use a different tokenization method (e.g., regex for word boundaries)?
If a word in mystrings contains underscores initially, should it still be replaced (e.g., 'hello_world' with spaces replaced by underscores might become 'hello__world')?
Does 'case-insensitive' apply only to the replacement operation, or also to the frequency counting (i.e., are 'Hello' and 'hello' considered the same word after modification)?
What should happen if mystrings contains duplicate entries? Should they be processed multiple times or deduplicated?
